data.title: Bose acquires Skullcandy in push to broaden audio brand portfolio
data.description:
Bose Corporation reached a deal to acquire fellow headphones brand Skullcandy, the companies formally announced on Oct. 21. The acquisition brings together two big names in consumer electronics and audio wearables, following a history of collaboration.

Bose is No. 103 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales. There, Skullcandy is No. 627.

data.title: David's Bridal plans to spin off its AI-powered Pearl platform
data.description:
In 2025, David’s Bridal’s Shopify transition paved the way for an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) reimagining of its Pearl wedding planner — and now, the company has plans to spin off Pearl as its own entity.

K&F Growth Acquisition Corp. II, as special purposed acquisition company, announced alongside David’s Bridal, that the two companies had signed a nonbinding letter of intent to carry out a process to that would see Pearl go public.

Ultimately, their plan also calls for Pearl to eventually own David’s Bridal’s brand and intellectual property.

David’s Bridal is No. 460 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

David’s Bridal is also No. 178 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

data.title: Parts Town Unlimited names new CIO and chief accounting officer to leadership team
data.description:
Equipment distributor Parts Town Unlimited named two new executives to its leadership team, including a chief information officer (CIO) to oversee its digital efforts.

The CIO role will belong to Pat Quint. Meanwhile, Kristi Belhumeur is taking on new duties as the company’s chief accounting officer.

The moves come more than a year after Parts Town CEO Bill Geary was named to the distributor’s top position. Geary noted the importance of both hires in a released statement.

Who is Parts Town Unlimited’s new CIO?

“Pat’s proven ability to turn technology into a strategic growth engine and unlock the full potential of AI-driven innovation, combined with Kristi’s deep expertise in multi-billion-dollar M&A transactions and finance transformation, makes them exceptional additions to our global leadership team,” said Geary. “Their leadership strengthens our ability to scale globally, accelerate growth and deepen the expertise needed to capitalize on new opportunities and drive long-term success.”

Most recently, Quint served in the CIO role at the global industrial manufacturing solutions provider Duravant. That followed a previous term as CIO at Mastronardi Produce.

Going forward, Parts Town Unlimited will look to Quint to execute its technology strategy. That strategy includes crucial automation and AI-powered technology, such as Parts Town’s PartPredictor tool, which received new features in 2026.

“It’s a privilege to work at Parts Town Unlimited given the impressive history, talented team, innovative solutions and focus on exceeding customer expectations,” Quint stated in Parts Town Unlimited’s announcement. “I look forward to helping the company achieve their goals by leveraging technology.”

Parts Town Unlimited’s chief accounting officer

Belhumeur, a certified public accountant, will bring 25 years of leadership experience in her field to Parts Town Unlimited. There, she will lead work for its global accounting, tax and treasury organizations, the company shared.

“Parts Town Unlimited has built an extraordinary business, and I look forward to applying my global finance leadership experience to help accelerate growth, support strategic expansion and deliver outstanding results for team members, customers and partners,” said Belhumeur.

Parts Town Unlimited noted that in addition to supporting mergers and acquisitions, Belhumeur will bolster audit and enterprise readiness at the company. She comes to Parts Town Unlimited after nearly two years as chief accounting officer at the janitorial supplies, foodservice, and industrial packaging distributor BradyPlus.

Parts Town Unlimited also serves the foodservice sector, in addition to its distribution of residential appliances and heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) equipment.

data.title: Amazon Business targets procurement efficiency with new AI and reporting features
data.description:
Almost one year after Amazon Business unveiled its Amazon Business Assistant in 2025, the business-to-business (B2B)-focused side of Amazon announced two ways in which it will seek to improve procurement for the buyers that it serves.

The new capabilities, revealed at the Amazon Business Reshape event in Nashville on Oct. 27, cover new Business Assistant enhancements, as well as an experience that the company refers to as Amazon Business Value Intelligence.

Both announcements include visibility and options aimed at procurement pain points in hopes of boosting Amazon Business sales.

What Amazon Business is adding to its procurement experience

Amazon characterized the new Business Assistant abilities as an expansion “from a general-purpose resource into a conversational tool that speaks to each customer’s business account orders, spend, and activity” in a blog post published Oct. 27.

“Every hour a procurement team spends chasing approvals or manually reconciling invoices is an hour they’re not spending on the work that moves their organization forward,” said Shelley Salomon, worldwide vice president of Amazon Business, in a released statement. “Amazon Business Assistant now steps in to handle the repetitive, time-consuming tasks that slow teams down, so they can focus on finding the right products, managing supplier relationships, and driving real value across their business.”

Specifically, the Business Assistant enhancements included order tracking, approvals process information, savings recommendations, integrated payment allocation options and spending analysis.

The features are available to Amazon Business customers in the U.S. through their account pages.

What is Amazon Business Value Intelligence?

Meanwhile, Amazon Business Value Intelligence will offer U.S.-based buyers new ways to understand savings, operational efficiency and purchase compliance. The information will be based on an organization’s own Amazon Business data, viewed alongside third-party benchmarks that Amazon Business tracks.

“Procurement has always been about more than price, but price is what gets reported because it’s the easiest thing to measure,” said Salomon. “We designed Value Intelligence to change the conversation from ‘what did this cost?’ to ‘what value is procurement creating?'”

Amazon Business is positioning Value Intelligence as a tool to communicate these outcomes to management and finance teams.

“Now leaders can see the savings, time back, and off-policy spend prevented in one view, and confidently show the full impact of their buying strategy, not just the price,” she stated.

The company pitched the features as means to lend credibility to strategy and decisions with data to support its conclusions. Ultimately, the intent is to provide procurement managers with reports that can be shared in their organizations so that finance teams can reconcile numbers and parties can align on stories about results and value being produced.

data.title: Walmart unveils AI agent shopping controls, spending limits
data.description:
Walmart wants its shoppers to stay in control as artificial intelligence (AI) agents take on a bigger role across ecommerce.

The retailer is rolling out new tools designed to let customers oversee AI agent purchases, streamline how agents shop and set boundaries for what they can and cannot do on shoppers’ behalf.

Announced Wednesday (Oct. 21), the changes are designed to support agentic commerce across Walmart and Sam’s Club. Walmart acknowledged that not everyone will want to shop using AI agents. But for those who do, the retailer said its goal is to “make our experience the most trusted” by building safeguards into the shopping process.

To support that, Walmart is introducing three updates:

  • Agent Profiles: To let shoppers authorize AI agents, set spending limits and track purchases.
  • Agent Gateway: For giving agents a more direct connection to Walmart’s shopping services.
  • New purchasing rules: Setting limits on agents’ actions and access to customer information.

Beyond changes for shoppers, Walmart is helping its marketplace sellers prepare for AI-driven product discovery, which could open up new opportunities to reach customers.

The move builds on Walmart’s existing AI shopping efforts. These include its Sparky AI shopping agent and integrations with Meta’s Muse, OpenAI ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini. The retailer has not specified which agents will support the new profiles at launch.

Walmart ranks No. 2 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Walmart is No. 37 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

How Walmart’s AI agent profiles will work

Walmart said it plans to launch Agent Profiles within the next month, giving shoppers a way to oversee AI-led purchases.

Currently, purchases made by AI agents appear alongside customers’ own orders in their Walmart accounts, with no way to tell them apart. The new feature will allow agents to “shop using dedicated profiles linked to a customer’s account, so customers can approve purchases, set spending limits, and see which purchases were made by an agent,” Daniel Danker, Walmart’s executive vice president of AI acceleration, product and design, said in a LinkedIn post.

Through Agent Profiles, shoppers can choose to approve AI purchases one at a time. Alternatively, they can allow agents to spend up to a preset limit, such as $50, $100 or $200.

The company outlined three steps for setting up an Agent Profile:

  • Start in the agent’s app: Walmart creates a profile when a customer first shops through its Agent Gateway.
  • Connect to Walmart: Customers sign in to their Walmart accounts to authorize and link the agent’s profile.
  • Set spending controls: Shoppers choose a spending limit, review purchases made by agents and can delete profiles at any time.

On Walmart’s website, agents will see “the same prices that a human would see,” with offers and fees displayed before purchase, the company noted.

What protections apply when AI agents shop?

Walmart is also “setting expectations for how AI agents work with customers and our company,” Danker said.

These safeguards come as consumers remain wary of giving AI control over purchases. In survey results published in August, payments technology provider NMI asked 1,000 U.S. adults about AI shopping. Only 11% of those surveyed reported using AI to complete a transaction. Meanwhile, 70% wanted the ability to review or override an AI purchasing decision before checkout. Only 10% said they would give AI full control over a purchase.

Addressing concerns, Walmart said its new terms require customers to approve agent purchases by default. Shoppers can authorize spending within preset limits, though the company said it could still require additional approval.

The rules also bar agents from acting beyond a shopper’s instructions, accessing unauthorized information or receiving payment-card details, according to Walmart. Additionally, agents cannot add or change payment methods.

If an agent makes an unintended purchase, Walmart said its existing returns process will apply. Agents that violate the terms will be blocked from its website.

Even so, information shoppers share directly with third-party AI apps remains subject to those providers’ privacy policies, the company said.

Walmart builds a direct connection for AI agents

Walmart is also developing the Agent Gateway, which gives AI systems a faster, more direct way to shop with the retailer.

Currently, agents use a browser to shop following steps designed for people. “This can be slow and error-prone, and agents may get stuck along the way,” Walmart said.

The Agent Gateway aims to address this using Model Context Protocol (MCP). The open standard developed by Anthropic allows AI applications to connect with external tools and services.

The gateway supports “discovery, add to cart, purchasing, and order tracking,” Danker said. It is also designed to help agents find products customers regularly buy without giving them access to sensitive customer information.

For example, Walmart said it could help an agent find a customer’s preferred brand of milk or bread “without sharing the customer’s broader shopping history.”

The gateway will launch in limited beta for companies and developers, though Walmart has not announced when or who will participate.

How agentic shopping could benefit Walmart Marketplace sellers

Agentic commerce is already changing how some Walmart shoppers find products, opening up new opportunities for marketplace sellers.

Speaking at Morgan Stanley’s Technology, Media and Telecom Conference in March, Danker said vitamin and protein supplements were the top two product types purchased from Walmart through ChatGPT. He suggested those purchases may have begun as broader conversations rather than searches for specific products.

That shift is a “potential game-changer” for sellers, said Manish Joneja, senior vice president of Walmart Global Marketplace and Walmart Fulfillment Services.

In a statement shared with Digital Commerce 360, Joneja said agentic commerce “could create more opportunities for sellers to put the right products in front of the right customers, including brands and products that may not have broad awareness.”

But it could also raise the bar for sellers. Joneja said accurate product information, competitive prices, availability and reliable delivery promises will all become increasingly important.

To prepare, Walmart is working with marketplace sellers to improve listings and catalog quality, he said. The changes will help make their products “easier for AI-powered shopping experiences to understand and recommend.”
